keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row for the British zone; it draws it inside the British Gold Coast shape from 1915 (74 Ghana cells and 9 Togo cells) and inside German Africa until 1914. The territory is the western part of German Togoland: occupied 27 August 1914, partitioned from French Togoland on 27 December 1916, a Class B mandate 20 July 1922 to 20 April 1946 and a UN trust territory 13 December 1946 to 6 March 1957. The page gives no area; the Togoland page gives 'approximately 90,400 km2' for the whole and 'about two-thirds and one-third' for the French and British zones, but Cliopatria's Ghana piece (79 cells) is about a quarter, so the region is a floor to be checked against a map. Second figure for the area (Togoland campaign page, opened 2026-10-25): 'The French acquisition consisted of about 60 per cent of the colony, including the coast' and the British received 'the smaller, less populated and less developed portion ... to the west', i.e. about 40 per cent or some 36,000 km2 of 90,400; the region here is about 20,000 km2 (22 per cent) and the ghana dossier's Volta Region about 25,500 km2 (28 per cent), so both are floors. Neither the British Togoland page (no area, no boundary, capital Ho) nor the Togoland campaign page gives the 27 December 1916 line or the Milner-Simon line of 1919; a map or a page of the line is still needed and the region is to be agreed with the ghana dossier's group.

Infobox 'Occupation: 27 August 1914'; the territory was 'effectively formed in 1916 by the splitting of the German protectorate of Togoland'. German title lasts until 28 June 1919, so the core of this state is occupied land: the compiler must draw it hatched (occupation_start below, same month) and not as direct land until then.

20 July 1922: British Togoland becomes a Class B League of Nations mandate (infobox '20 July 1922 - 20 April 1946').
13 December 1946: the territory becomes a UN Trust Territory (infobox '13 December 1946 - 6 March 1957').

certainty.note: A wartime occupation line; the page does not give the boundary between the Anglo-French zones before the partition of 27 December 1916.

The Anglo-French zone line of the partition (1916), confirmed by the mandate (1922) and the trusteeship (1946); the page names no coordinates, so the line follows the gazetteer's Ghana part of the Togoland shape.

notes:
Written by af-08-c as a direct counterpart of german-africa and british-gold-coast that no Cliopatria row covers (the ghana dossier flagged it as needing a dossier). Three pages opened (British Togoland, German Togoland, Gold Coast); no more were needed for the territory's few dated steps.

The territory is the Ghana part of Cliopatria's 1914 German Togoland shape (79 cells), which is about a quarter of the colony by cell count, not the 'one third' the German Togoland page implies for the British zone; Cliopatria's Togoland piece in Ghana is therefore probably short, and the ghana dossier's Volta Region (101 cells, of which 52 were already Gold Coast Colony in 1900 by Cliopatria's British Gold Coast shape) is wider. A gap-filler with a map of the 1916 line should settle the region. Cliopatria draws the territory in the British Gold Coast shape from 1915 (and drops it in 1917, a one-year glitch).

Model: the British zone is occupied German land (hatched over german-africa) from 27 August 1914; German title ends with the Treaty of Versailles (28 June 1919), after which it is a British mandate (20 July 1922), a UN trust territory (13 December 1946) and part of Ghana (6 March 1957). The Gold Coast shows it as a dependency (vassal events, 27 December 1916 to December 1956). No Cliopatria shapes, so there is a single new keyframe; no rulers. Wikidata id: none known (Cliopatria has no row).

Repairs of 2026-10-25 (review af-08-c). (1) Added the mirror vassal_start (27 December 1916) and vassal_end (13 December 1956) with counterpart british-gold-coast, as the Gold Coast dossier books them. (2) The found event, the occupation_start and the 1919 gain still book the same 79 cells; the found note now says that the core is occupied land and must be drawn hatched until 28 June 1919. The alternative (start the state on 27 December 1916, 'effectively formed in 1916') was not taken because the occupation of 27 August 1914 is dated by the infobox. Orchestrator to confirm that the compiler lets occupation_start override a found region. (3) The region still stands at 79 cells; the Togoland campaign page gives the French about 60 per cent of the colony (British about 40 per cent, some 36,000 km2) against 20,000 km2 here and 25,500 km2 for the Volta Region, and no page opened gives the line; the flag for the ghana dossier's group stands. (4) The german-africa dossier now books the owner side of the occupation (occupation_start 1914/8, occupation_end 1919/6, counterpart british-togoland).
